title: Abuse
description: Abuse is a great side-scrolling action game that uses a unique system to control your character. You use the keyboard to move around and the mouse to aim your gun. It works pretty well and the game can be great fun to play, since it has nicely done graphics and sound effects, as well as many non-linear levels and powerups. (Also check out the fan-made project based on the original source code, fRaBs!) Video ReviewVideo review of Abuse, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: DOOM
description: Chosen by Computer Gaming World as part of their 'Hall of Fame' ("DOOM revolutionized PC action games"), and at (or near) the top of many "best of" game lists, DOOM is one of the most played computer games of all time. And for good reason! I admit, it scared the hell outta me when I first played it. Even today, with increasingly sophisticated 3D action games DOOM's gameplay is classic. Get it now, even if you've already played it ... it's still fun. But just in case you've never played it before (play it now!) this game was revolutionary because of both its technical prowess and its amazing game design by a team of supremely talented developers at id Software. You play as a space marine who needs to shoot up a bunch of demons and stuff. (Not the "official" storyline but pretty much all you need to know.) The game has an amazing "feel" that leads to people still playing it enthusiastically even today. It helped that a huge modding community started making new maps for it, and even total conversions. The game just celebrated its 25th birthday as of December 2018! Video ReviewVideo review of DOOM, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Super Street Fighter II Turbo
description: Street Fighter II first came to DOS PCs in 1992, with an absolutely terrible port of the original game Street Fighter II: The World Warrior. Thankfully, this version is way better than the original port, making this game quite close to the arcade and console versions of the game. If you've played SF2 before, you know what to expect: One-on-one fighting of the highest quality. Great graphics, sound effects, and music round out the package. Of course using the keyboard to perform special moves is mediocre at best so you'd probably want a joystick or arcade setup if you're interested in playing this for real. The demo version allows play as Ryu and Chun Li only, and while two-player shared keyboard play is available in the full version, the demo is one player only.

title: Prince of Persia
description: Prince of Persia is a classic platforming game developed by Jordan Mechner. It premiered Jordan's use of the "rotoscoping" technique to digitize lifelike movements of the in-game characters. The game itself is a race against time since the clock is always ticking down, but moreso against all of the various traps and high falls in the dungeon which kill you just as much as the enemy characters that you will encounter. As an in-game text file included with the demo states: "It's like an Arabian Nights movie come to life... with you as the star!" The controls do take some getting used to, but they became standard for this sort of game, as also seen in the sequel Prince of Persia: The Shadow and the Flame, as well as other later games like Blackthorne or Out of this World. The graphics are indeed very appealing, as the movements of the characters and other in-game elements feel like they have real weight to them. Try this demo version out to see how you like the original game that inspired the modern 3D series!

title: Wolfenstein 3D
description: Although there were 3D games on the PC before Wolfenstein 3D (one notable example was Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss), it was this game by iD Software which brought 3D gaming to the masses. It was a simple game: Get to the end of the level, killing Nazis on the way. But it became ridiculously popular because of its fast, fluid gameplay, violence, and its 3D engine which would run on most reasonably recent PCs at the time without the need for a 3D graphics card. (The official source code was released by id Software, see link above to download it.) Video ReviewVideo review of Wolf3D, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Simcity
description: This time-limited demo version of the original Simcity shows off a little of what made the game so revolutionary at the time. The game does not play like a traditional video game in the sense that there is no definite "win" condition; your goal is to simply build the best city that you can. The series began a whole line of "Sim" games which were essentially sandbox titles. The original is simple compared to other games in the series but part of its charm is the simplicity which makes it easy to learn. The graphics are serviceable, and while there is no background music, the simple PC speaker sound effects are quite memorable. Video ReviewVideo review of Simcity, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Prehistorik 2
description: Prehistorik 2 is a platforming game with simple controls and gameplay, but a lot of polish. You are a caveman and need to bonk enemies with your club and collect everything you see for POINTS. The graphics are well-done and the game controls quite smoothly, with the exception being that instead of scrolling smoothly, the levels scroll in screen-sized increments. It's a bit disorienting but not game-breaking. This demo version was updated, perhaps by one of its original programmers, ripsaw8080, to work in DOSBox. It's definitely worth trying out.

title: Disney's Aladdin
description: This demo version of the wonderfully animated game based on the 1992 Disney movie Aladdin (sometimes misspelled Alladin) gives you a taste of what the full game offers. You of course play Aladdin, and you must platform your way through many levels based on scenes from the iconic movie, including the bazaar, caves, and palace. As you might expect from a Disney-based game, the graphics, sounds, and MOD-like music are great, and the controls are responsive and work well for this type of game. It doesn't feel like a forced movie-based cash-in game, but rather a natural extension of the world created by the popular movie.

title: Doom The Roguelike
description: Making the famous DOOM 3D shooting game into a RogueLike, turn-based RPG game with text "graphics" sounds like the recipe for disaster. But this RPG based on the original DOOM games (actually referred to as DRL, I suppose due to copyright concerns) actually plays very well. While more simplistic than games like Nethack or ADOM, DRL focuses more on combat (of course!) and weaponry, so it is faster paced than more traditional RogueLike games. Quite innovative and surprisingly good, a definite must-play for fans of the text-based RPG subgenre. (There are also more recent releases available for Windows, Linux, and OSX on the official site.)

title: Tetris
description: The original version of Tetris, as conceived by Alexey Pajitnov and coded in part by Vadim Gerasimov, this is how it all began! (Gerasimov has released the game for free on the web.) The story of Tetris is long and complicated (see the superb hour long video by the Video Game Historian, The Story of Tetris, to learn all about it!) but the game itself is deceptively simple. If you owned an original Gameboy, chances are you played this! This version of the original includes many of the options familiar to us from later versions including Nintendo's. Gerasimov notes that this version was done in text mode in order to be compatible with the widest variety of machines available at the time. (If you're looking for more elaborate Tetris games with better graphics, more features, etc, check out our Tetris-style games category for plenty of options!)

title: Duke Nukem 3D
description: Does blowing away pigcops, destroying entire buildings, and shooting your way through an adult XXX store sound enjoyable? Then you'll love Duke 3D. It uses the "Build" engine, which is still similar to the old Wolf3D engine in that there are no rooms on top of other rooms, but the Build engine includes many new features, like walls of different heights and angles, lighting effects, and a versatile scripting system. Lots of fun! The first of several games using Ken Silverman's versatile engine, Duke Nukem 3D gets a lot right and has just the right "feel", especially in the introductory shareware episode. You can tell that a lot of time and care went into this release. (Note: Several people have emailed me to comment that there ARE rooms-above-rooms in Duke3D. While the effect of rooms-above-rooms can be _simulated_ in Build, there are never really any rooms on top of other rooms in the game, and thus it's not truly 3D.) Video ReviewVideo review of Duke Nukem 3D, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: 3D Bomber
description: 3D Bomber is a 3D version of Bomberman. You can play against the computer, or with a human opponent via modem or null modem cable. (Not sure how viable that is nowadays so you may need to be content with the single player game.) The game plays similarly to the classic Bomberman game, except that all the action takes place in a 3D first-person perspective, Wolfenstein 3D type environment. As you might except, it's rather difficult to navigate the maze-like level when you can only see what's directly around you. You can't plan and strategically go after your opponent. The author probably realized this because there is a tiny mini-map added to the bottom corner which is barely visible. In practice, you'll need to try to use this to see where your opponent is. However that means that the 3D element becomes almost superfluous.

title: Descent
description: Descent was quite popular on its release. It expanded on the 3D shooting genre by giving players a real 3D environment unlike Doom or Duke Nukem 3D. In this 7-level DEMO version of Descent you must pilot your spaceship through many 3D levels destroying various bad guys along the way. Think of Doom crossed with Wing Commander and you'll have a fairly good picture of what this game's about. A fun shooter that has aged pretty well (and still works on my XP computer) that lacks a bit of the flair and style of Doom or Duke Nukem 3D. title: Rayman
description: This four-level demo version of the original Rayman game shows off the whimsical graphical style and engaging gameplay of the first game in the series. A villain known as Mr. Dark has captured Rayman's friends, and it's up to you to save them as you travel through platforming levels filled with gorgeous graphics and fluid animations. Rayman has no arms or legs, but he does have hands and feet, which he can use to defeat enemies and grab onto things. You will of course also find powerups along the way. The controls are tight and responsive, and this game is a great introduction to the series which is tons of fun. If you are only familiar with the Rabbids, give the original game a try! For a PC game in 1995 it holds its own compared to the console games of the time.

title: Deluxe Ski Jump
description: Deluxe Ski Jump is a great ski jump simulation game. The game's sequels are still continuing to this day, ie Deluxe Ski Jump 4 on the author's website. The original DOS version of the game isn't in 3D like the modern versions but it's still fun and well done, albeit simple since you're doing basically the same thing every time. Using the mouse, begin your jump, time your leap from the end of the take-off board and then carefully adjust in the air before performing your landing. It takes a few tries to get right but it's not too difficult. The shareware version includes four different jump locations.

title: Blockout
description: Blockout is one of the best Tetris sequel that is not an official Tetris release. It's basically Tetris in 3D. Instead of looking at the well from the side, you look down into it, and rotate and place all of the pieces in 3D. It's a bit tricky to get used to, but many consider this game one of the definitive (albeit unofficial) iterations of the original Tetris formula. Welltris is the official 3D version and honestly I'm not sure how they differ, but Blockout seems to be the better known of the two. (This game has been released by permission of Kadon Enterprises Inc (who are copyright holders of the Blockout name) on the Blockout.net website. Visit the Kadon website GamePuzzles.com for many interesting and fun puzzle games.) There is also an online version with a global high scores board by Magnus Ivarsson available at Blockout.nu.

title: Alone In The Dark
description: Anyone who has played the Resident Evil or other modern "survival horror" games should really take a look at Alone in the Dark. It was "inspired by the work of H. P. Lovecraft". In the game, your character investigates a strange house with holds many surprises (and sometimes jump scares). It turns out, as many of you probably already know/remember, the basic mechanics used in Resident Evil were pioneered by Alone in the Dark. Its graphics, while hightech at the time of its release, look rather poor now, but remember, this was many years BEFORE 3D cards. Overall it's still a fun game to play, and the classic game that spawed the entire "survival horror" genre. (NOTES: This is the demo version of the full game. To start the game, run the file "tatou.com". Press 'S' during the game to turn on sound effects.)

title: One Must Fall 2097
description: One Must Fall 2097 is a futuristic one-on-one fighting game in the style of other popular fighting games of the time such as Street Fighter II, Mortal Kombat, and numerous others. Upon release, the game was praised for its graphics, smooth gameplay mechanics, and innovative features. Based on the game developer's initial demo, this game takes place far in the future, with mech-like robots fighting each other. There are several game modes: One player vs computer, two player competitive combat, or tournament mode. The last mode is the most innovative: You start by creating your own character to pilot your robot, then gain experience and new powers as you defeat other robots. Sort of like some minor RPG mechanics. Graphically, the game looks good for its time, and the music is pumping, as long as you like early 90's techno! Not the best fighting game ever, but certainly one of the best made for PCs in the 90's. (The game's developer, Diversions Entertainment, released the game as freeware back in 2003 so the download available on DOSGames.com is the full version of the game. A remake project which is open source, OpenOMF, also exists for Windows / other modern OSes.) Video ReviewVideo review of One Must Fall 2097, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Warcraft 2: Tides of Darkness
description: Blizzard's follow-up sequel to their successful Warcraft: Orcs & Humans RTS game was immensely successful, and people still continue to play it today. Warcraft II continues the same style as its predecessor, but adds numerous features and innovations which make it a superior game to the original. Again you choose to play as either the humans or the orcs, and battle against the other. You can play against a human opponent over a local network or the Internet, or you can play against the computer. The graphics are detailed and well drawn, and the sound effects and music are classic ("Zug zug!"). This shareware version (I would've called it a demo but it clearly says shareware on the title screen) includes six unique maps not found in the full game, as well as one demo multiplayer map. title: Simcity 2000
description: Simcity 2000 is of course the sequel to the immensely popular Simcity which Maxis released a few years earlier in 1989. This demo version of the sequel (limited to 20 minutes of playing time) keeps many of the same gameplay mechanics as the original, but also improves the graphics and sounds while implementing new mechanics to build your own cities. You are again the mayor of a new city, and your task is to grow it into a healthy metropolis. There are of course many new buildings that you can create such as zoos and hospitals. The land is now no longer completely flat, so you may need to do some terraforming to be able to place things where you want them. Some of the new mechanics seem a bit unnecessary and tedious (such as the water system) while other such as the newspapers provided to gauge how your city is doing are nice additions. Generally speaking a great sequel to the original, although the original game is still a better choice for a more casual experience.

description: Micro Machines received good reviews upon its original release, especially for the NES. The concept is that you are racing the tiny "Micro Machine" brand cars around typical locations like a table, where items like pencils and notebooks become huge obstacles on the race track. The PC version features fast and furious gameplay along with decent aesthetics. The action may be too frantic, actually, since it's difficult to control your car. I'm not exactly sure what speed the original game is supposed to run at, but at any speed, navigating the course is challenging, especially when the computer opponents don't seem to have any trouble with it!

title: Sam & Max: Hit the Road

This is one of the classic Lucasarts games, coming around the same time as other classics like Day of the Tentacle. The story involves the two protagonists traveling across America to solve their case. Along the way you will encounter numerous puzzles that you solve via the Lucasarts point-and-click adventure interface, as well as a few mini games. The game excels in its irreverent humor and the dialogue between Sam and Max and other characters. The graphics, music, and sound effects are all top-notch, so be sure to check out this game if you're a fan of graphical adventure games. title: Where in the USA is Carmen Sandiego?
description: After the runaway success of the original release of Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego? software developer BrÃ¸derbund Software of course began to release sequels. The demo version of Where in the USA is Carmen Sandiego? available here seems to present a single case for investigation, while of course the full version contains many more. The premise and gameplay are the same as the other early games in the series: A thief has run off with an item of value, and it's your job to track them down. To do so, you'll travel to various places in the United States to look for clues. The actual game came with some nice manuals and information about the different areas. Intended as a learning game for kids, I'm not sure how much we actually learned from them, but they were definitely fun to play!

title: Clockwiser
description: Clockwiser is an inventive and now free puzzle game. Originally a commercial product, the game has graciously been released for free by its original developers. Racing against the clock, you must draw rectangles and rotate blocks clockwise (or counter-clockwise) to make the blocks on the left side of the screen match the blocks on the right side. It includes over 200 levels and later levels introduce new mechanics, like gravity, teleporters, and bombs. The game plays quite well (you can use keyboard or mouse, the latter of which is recommended) and looks good too. Definitely a hidden gem that you should try out. The main disadvantage is that you'll need to use the copy-protection sheet included in the ZIP file (Clockwiser load-up matrix) to solve the copy protection challenge.

description: Elder Scrolls: Daggerfall is the second game in the Elder Scrolls series which later spawned the more recent Elder Scrolls games. It's a first-person view 3D RPG that was once called "best CRPG of the year" and "a flawed masterpiece" by Computer Games Magazine (link). Daggerfall is an open-world game fan's dream as it allows you to roam freely and do what you want in it's huge world. The world is said to be 62,394 square miles in size. For comparison, that is approximately 4000 times as large as Oblivion's world! (See this map, with Daggerfall's size listed on the side.) It's quite amazing a world so large was packed into a file so relatively small (149 megs). The full version of this game was released for free by its owner. Video ReviewVideo review of Elder Scrolls: Daggerfall, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Bio Menace
description: Bio Menace is a decent EGA platformer from Apogee. It's got some nice EGA graphics and SoundBlaster sounds, though, as well as a few original elements like interaction with the game's backgrounds. It has a unique style, and it encourages more thoughtful and planned playing rather than running around shooting everything. For whatever reason, however, it doesn't seem quite as fun as some of Apogee's other games. (Note that this is the full registered version of this game, which was released as freeware by 3D Realms.) title: Commander Keen 4: Secret of the Oracle
description: Commander Keen Secret of the Oracle is the well-received fourth episode in the Commander Keen series. (The series this game is part of is called "Goodbye Galaxy!") Like the original game, it was developed by iD Software and published by Apogee. In this game, Billy "Commander Keen" Blaze is again called into action and must adventure into an overhead map and then into platforming stages. The main complaint against this game (as with the original) would probably the one-hit-death mechanics, which can make each level feel more stressful as you near the exit! However this game improves on the graphics, music, and sound effects of the earlier games while including many of the same elements that made the original successful (such as the pogo stick) and provides a fun experience. (It even includes an epic game of Pong, aka "Paddle War", on the main menu ...)

title: Space Invaders
description: Space Invaders is not surprisingly a clone of the classic Space Invaders arcade game. This one is not made by Taito, rather by Paul S Reid, who was at the time working on a comp sci diploma, as per the included docs. It's a decent approximation of the arcade, although there are no sounds and every time your ship gets destroyed, the aliens all respawn, which is not how it worked in the arcade AFAIK. Still a decent attempt which works more or less like you'd expect, and it's impressive that the executable file is so tiny.

title: Alien Rampage
description: Alien Rampage has no connection to either the "Alien(s)" nor the "Rampage" franchises. It's a great looking 2D platform shooting game. (But it's not Alien Carnage, a game by Apogee Software/3D Realms. Lots of games with Alien in the name!) The game's graphics and animations, as well as the abnormally large sprites including your own character, add greatly to the experience. The storyline doesn't really matter; your objective is to run through the levels, finding secrets and gathering bonuses and powerups, all while blowing away all of the enemies in your way. You do find coins which can be used to buy things. The game is rather bloody, with many enemies exploding into a bloody burst when killed.

title: Snood
description: Even though Snood was basically a weird looking takeoff of the popular Puzzle Bobble or Bust-A-Move, it became extremely popular for a time. The object, like Puzzle Bobble, is to rotate your turret at the bottom of the screen and shoot colored "Snoods" to try to connect three or more of the same color. The Snoods themselves are rather ugly face-blocks of different colors. Every time you shoot a Snood and don't make a three-or-more connection the Danger meter increases, and when it's full the screen drops by one. The graphics are detailed (high-res 640x480 mode) and certainly distinct, but strange, and the gameplay is classic but also a bit simple by today's standards.

title: Dangerous Dave in Copyright Infringement
description: This is not so much a game as it is a tech demo, but what a tech demo it was back in 1990. Future id Software superstar John Carmack created a way to have smooth scrolling EGA graphics, which was a brand new thing back then. Together with Tom Hall they put together a quick demo to showcase the new technology which was dubbed "Dangerous Dave in Copyright Infringement". See this article by John Romero about the game for more information about the game's development. (Or the great book Masters of Doom about the history of id Software.) It's not much fun as a GAME (there's only one "level", no enemies, the question mark blocks don't work ...) but it's still very neat to play as a piece of video game history, or even as a parody of sorts of the classic NES Mario games. (It also includes the TED level editor that Romero created.)

title: Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss
description: Ultima Underworld was a revolutionary game when it was released, introducing new features to the RPG genre including real-time 3D graphics which even in some ways surpassed Doom (released the next year in 1993). In this demo version you will get a small taste of what the full game offers, namely an intricately designed and developed RPG with a large "dungeon crawl" to explore, many NPC characters to meet and converse with, and excellent atmosphere. Overall it exudes the time and effort that went into making it a classic game and one that heavily influenced PC RPGs for many years after it was released.

title: Quake
description: One of the best DOS games ever? Probably! Released as the long-awaited follow up to iD Software's classic DOOM, Quake had high expectations. In most ways, I think it met them. Or at least it met mine. It added fully 3D levels, cool new weapons and enemies, and ultra-fast frantic gameplay. And a lot of the color brown. I have spent many hours playing this classic, and still go back to play it sometimes. If you have never played it ... get it now! With the release of Quake, iD Software once again revolutionized the 3D shooting genre. It's great, even today! Video ReviewVideo review of Quake, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Bolo Ball
description: Bolo Ball is a simple but interesting strategy game intended for one player vs the computer. (There doesn't seem to be a multiplayer option.) The object is to strategically choose which of your 29 balls to push down the playing field. The farther your ball bounces down, the more points you get. As the playing field changes during the game, your decisions may become less obvious. It's a fun and fairly unique little game, with the usual Soleau Software style EGA graphics and basic PC speaker sound effects.

title: Hexxagon
description: An extremely enjoyable puzzle game. It's quite similar to Reversi/Othello, except with a hexagon grid rather than a square grid. The object is to take over the gameboard (which can be edited by the user and saved) with marbles (gems?) of your own color. It includes a single player vs. computer option (with three skill levels) and also a two player option. Definitely fun to play, as it's got a really nice looking interface, and, on the 'easy' setting, I can sometimes actually win! :)

description: As soon as you run this game, you can tell it's going to be an experience that's higher quality than your average shareware game. The VGA graphics in this sidescrolling Mario-esque jumping game are very nice, and there are some SB sound effects too. (Unfortunately no music.) The gameplay consists of just getting to the next level. Probably influenced by the Great Giana Sisters (which itself was highly "influenced" by Mario). Charlie the Duck is quite fun to play, although unforgiving, so plan your jumps carefully!

title: Where in Europe is Carmen Sandiego?
description: After the runaway success of the original release of Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego? software developer Brøderbund Software of course began to release sequels. The demo version of Where in Europe is Carmen Sandiego? available here seems to present a single case for investigation, while of course the full version contains many more. The premise and gameplay are the same as the other early games in the series: A thief has run off with an item of value, and it's your job to track them down. To do so, you'll travel to various places in Europe to look for clues. The actual game came with some nice manuals and information about the different areas. Intended as a learning game for kids, I'm not sure how much we actually learned from them, but they were definitely fun to play!

title: Raptor: Call of the Shadows
description: I remember playing this for far too long. It's a fairly basic shooting game (gameplay-wise), however, it has nice looking graphics and SB sound effects. As you earn money for each enemy that you blast, you can use the cash to buy upgrades for your ship. This helps to give you an incentive to keep playing and collecting more money and more upgrades to power up your ship. It's enjoyable if you just feel like blasting stuff. It has a very good "feel" to it which has made it a favorite in the shoot-em-up genre. Video ReviewVideo review of Raptor, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Terminal Velocity

(It gets much tougher during the later levels, however.) I found it to be a lot of fun, even though it gets very challenging. The open-ended feeling of flying around is not often found in games of this era. Impressive what could be done back then without the aid of any kind of 3D graphics card! title: Beyond Castle Wolfenstein
description: Beyond Castle Wolfenstein is a free release of an originally commercial game which was released for free after the death of its author. ("After the death of Silas Warner in 2004, the reconstructed source code and a ported version of the game was released for free by his widow in honor of him.") The original Castle Wolfenstein of course helped inspire Wolfenstein 3D, one of the most well-known early FPS games. This is the sequel to Castle Wolfenstein, and is in fact a fan-made conversion of the PC booter to a native DOS program. It retains the complexity of the original game; see the instructions below for the myriad of keys required to play! Definitely not an easy game to jump into but I'm sure some people will enjoy it.

title: Duke Nukem
description: One of my all-time favorite action platformers. It just has excellent level design, items, enemies, and interactivity. This is the first appearance of Duke Nukem, who would go on to further fame in his 3D series of games. In the original game he has a little less attitude but the outline of the character he would become is definitely here. The graphics look good (for EGA, that is). (Fun fact: Many of the game's sprites were directly ripped off from other games.) And even though the sounds are played through the PC speaker, they aren't that annoying! Overall this is a tremendously fun game that's definitely worth the download! Video ReviewVideo review of Duke Nukem, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Ragnarok
description: Another "roguelike" role-playing game (called "Valhalla" in some regions), Ragnarok gets extra points for using actual graphics instead of the usual ASCII characters used in most other similar games. The gameplay of Ragnarok involves exploring the gameworld, building experience, collecting items, etc ... all of which (like Rogue, Nethack, etc.) are randomly generated each time you begin a new game. The story is also a bit deeper than most games of this type, and you can use your mouse to control some aspects of the game. The motif is also unique, with a Viking/Norse (Scandinavian) mythology rather than the typical fantasy tropes.

title: Freddy Pharkas: Frontier Pharmacist
description: Freddy Pharkas: Frontier Pharmacist is one of the games that Al Lowe was the primary writer for during his time at Sierra. Besides of course the Leisure Suit Larry series. This demo version of the full graphic adventure game highlights the mouse-driven interface of the later Sierra titles, shared by other games of the time such as Space Quest IV. This game takes place during the gold rush era, and as usual you click around, die frequently, and eventually give up and use a hint guide. Sierra didn't produce many playable demos for their games; not sure why this one was chosen! But from what I've read it's an enjoyable game with rather obscure and inane puzzles that will perhaps have you reaching for that hint guide sooner than other games. (Note: I wasn't able to get the sound working in DOSBox, so I chose PC speaker in the setup program. Run SETUP.EXE and try your luck if you want working SoundBlaster or other sounds; you may need to play with DOSBox's options to get it working.)

title: Simon the Sorcerer
description: Simon the Sorcerer is a classic graphical adventure game, and one of the few well-known games of its type from its time that was not released by Sierra or Lucasarts. The plot follows the titular Simon, an average English boy who ends up being teleported into a magical land and must become a sorcerer's apprentice. The style of the game is quite similar to Lucasarts titles such as Secret of Monkey Island, in both gameplay and its comedic tone. There are numerous parodies of fairytales in the game. Generally speaking the game features great graphics and music, as well as an enjoyable puzzle-solving experience. Try this demo version to see if you like it before buying the full version! (Apparently the version on GOG.com is not good; try buying it from the original publisher instead.)

title: Cannon Fodder
description: Cannon Fodder is an action-oriented strategy game where you control a team of up to six soldiers on various missions. Use the mouse to move your team and fight your enemies on the way to completing your objectives. The game has decent graphics, although since it's a Sensible Software title the characters are rendered as tiny sprites on the screen! While not as in-depths as most strategy titles or as action-packed as many of the best action games, Cannon Fodder's hybrid gameplay landed it as one of the "1001 Video Games You Must Play Before You Die" book. The full game has 72 levels of combat, although this version is the "shareware" version (re)published by MVP Software has significantly less. Video ReviewVideo review of Cannon Fodder, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Balloon Challenge
description: Balloon Challenge is a puzzle game with much in common with several of Soleau Software's other similar EGA/VGA puzzle games, but with some unique rules of its own. The object is to get your balloons as high as possible on the game board. After choosing a balloon, it will float up the screen, and change directions based on what it hits. So you must choose your balloons carefully! Not tremendously exciting but there is an element of strategy to the game and the playing field will be different every time that you play. Don't try to play with your friends, however, since there is no mutliplayer mode; you can only play against the computer.

title: Earthworm Jim 1 & 2: The Whole Can O' Worms
description: The Earthworm Jim games are gaming classics, most famous on the 16-bit consoles (SNES and Genesis) but the games were also available for computer platforms such as DOS, WIndows, and Mac. The verbosely titled "Earthworm Jim 1 & 2: The Whole Can O' Worms" is a collection of both of the first two games in a single package. All of the great animation and sounds from the games are here, as well as the levels. Unlike many early PC ports, the Earthworm Jim games translated very well to PCs. Run and gun in this demo version that offers levels from both games. Run EJW1.EXE and EJW2.EXE to play the demos of the first and second games, respectively. Note: Due to a weird glitch in the browser-based version, you must complete the setup process before playing! But if you download and run the game from your own PC, you shouldn't have that issue.

title: Quarantine
description: Quarantine is a futuristic taxi simulation game that predates the Crazy Taxi and Grand Theft Auto series by several years. The game takes place in the gritty futuristic prison city Kemo. The goal is simply to pick up passengers and deliver them to their destinations to earn cash to buy better upgrades for your car. There are missions in the full game, but in this demo you get one of five city districts to explore and pick up passengers, but you can't progress in the game beyond buying new weapons and such. Decent graphics and innovative gameplay for the time.

title: Duke Nukem II
description: Between the original, classic Duke and the kickass Duke Nukem 3D came the unheralded sequel, Duke II. (Which really would've been Duke 4, if you counted the "registered-only" episodes 2 and 3.) The main advantages of the sequel over the original are in the areas of its graphics (in-game graphics, besides the introduction and some cutscenes, are still EGA, but they look better) and sound (SB instead of the PC speaker). It looks and sounds great, and the game is a bit more linear and action-focused compared to the exploration-heavy original game. However, despite the cool new effects, it doesn't seem quite as fun as the original. (There is a great recreation of the Duke II game engine for Windows, Mac, and Linux called Rigel Engine which allows wide-screen play at 60fps and several other nice features, so if you're playing on those platforms try it out! It needs a copy of the game to work.) Video ReviewVideo review of Duke Nukem 2, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

You also get to drive vehicles on some levels of the full game.

title: Emerald Hunt
description: Emerald Hunt is a Boulderdash-inspired puzzle/strategy game with randomized levels. The goal of course is to collect as many emeralds as possible. Your bulldozer can plow through the dirt to reach them, however watch out for falling boulders that can crush you, and enemies that can kill you. The randomized levels mean that each time you play is different, although since the game is very simple each game will quickly start to feel similar since the different objects are literally strewn randomly around the map. The map is quite large and there are a lot of emeralds to collect, so finishing even one level will be a challenge.

title: Terminator: Rampage
description: Terminator: Rampage is a 3D shooting game from Bethesda, one of several in their early/mid 90's line of Terminator FPS games. Compared to some of the other games in the series, it's not quite up to the same level. The engine is a bit clunky (the game was released just before DOOM but is technically way behind) and the turning speed feels exceedingly slow compared to how fast you move forwards. The level design feels like a confusing maze with walls that are all the same color. There are enemies to fight, and each pops up an information box when you target them which is nice, but really you treat each the same way and shoot them until they blow up.

One of Apogee's later products, this game has all the markings of Apogee's other quality games.

title: The Blues Brothers
description: The Blues Brothers, a game based on the Dan Aykroyd and John Belushi Saturday Night Live comedic duo, is a platforming game produced by European developer Titus. The game has nice graphics and sounds, with the graphics having that certain European flavor. You can choose to play as either Jake or Elwood in this demo version of the full five-level game. You have no weapons, but you can pick up and throw crates (ala Super Mario Bros 2, which was released a few years earlier on the NES) to defeat foes that come after you. A decent licensed game.

title: Alien Trilogy
description: Alien Trilogy is a FPS based on the popular movie series that was released the same year as Quake. It is not as polished or impressive as Quake but is a great game in its own right. You play as Lt. Ripley and work your way through sections based on each of the original Alien films. You'll shoot all of the aliens you see from the movies through intricately designed space-type locations. The environments feel a bit cramped compared to Quake's more open world but there is plenty of action here, with weapons to find and many doors to activate via switches. This demo version provides the entire first level of the full game.

title: Out of this World (Another World)
description: Out of this World (aka Another World) is a early polygon based action/adventure game which featured a distinctive artistic style and trial-and-error based gameplay which could be rather frustrating, yet the game was certainly memorable and entertaining. You play a scientist who has accidentally been sent to "another world" and must figure out what to do in order to survive. The side-view gameplay feels quite a bit like Prince of Persia, but the gameplay revolves more around simple puzzles. Unless you're using a walkthough, you will undoubtedly die many times as you attempt to figure out where to go and what to do. Later games like Flashback (also made by Delphine) and Blackthorne by Blizzard expanded on this style of game and added additional features, but this was the first. I suspect its artistic style continues to impact games today, especially in the indie scene.

title: Commander Keen 1: Invasion of the Vorticons
description: This is the first game (the shareware one) in the original Commander Keen series, "Commander Keen in Invasion of the Vorticons". (This episode's subtitle is "Marooned on Mars".) I thought that this game was SO amazing when I first played it (many years ago), and it's still quite fun now. It features great graphics (for EGA) and some not-so-annoying PC speaker sound effects. At the time, it was quite innovative due to the way that the screen smoothly scrolls. The engine was originally pitched to Nintendo for a PC Mario game, but since that never happened, Commander Keen was born to make use of it. The jumping and pogo-sticking (yes, that's a word) take a bit of getting used to ... otherwise, a great, classic Apogee platformer which spawned numerous sequels and an unofficial "mascot" for this website. :) Video ReviewVideo review of Commander Keen, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Sopwith
description: A true classic! :) Despite its CGA 4-color graphics, Sopwith is a game that many of you have probably played at one time or another. In this game you fly your plane around a landscape, and use your guns and bombs to blow up targets on the ground and in the air. It's still good fun if you look past the dated graphics/sounds! This is the "Network Edition" but don't ask me how to get it working over a network. (Note: This version is slightly modified from the original by the original author of the game so that it will work with modern computers.) More info and downloads of other versions are available on the sopwith.org website. NOTE! Controls: X starts the engine, then press , to go up, / to go down, Spacebar to fire, and B to drop bombs.

title: Epic Pinball
description: My favorite computer pinball games! The shareware version only contains one table, but it's really cool. Great graphics, smooth scrolling, SB sounds, and "good enough" physics. The screen scrolls to follow the ball, and while it's unfortunate that you never get to see the entire table at once, it allows for more detail to be shown on the screen. The shareware version includes a single table, Android (in later versions "Super Android"). It's really fun to play, and remember that a computer pinball game can do stuff you never could with a physical table. Ordering the whole collection from Epic (or more likely today, finding a digital copy online) would be worth it. Video ReviewVideo review of Epic Pinball, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

Released approximately two years after their earlier (and more well-known) games, Extreme Pinball was also released for the Sony Playstation. In this demo version, you get the "Rock Fantasy" table, which is one of the four tables included in the full version of the game. The action is fast-paced (perhaps slightly too fast at times) but I guess that's what makes it EXTREME! (The 90's were all about extreme-ness.) Generally good graphics and a rockin soundtrack make this a fun pinball game to play, even if the physics aren't the most accurate.

title: DreamWeb
description: Dreamweb is an unusual fully overhead perspective graphical adventure game. This dystopian future game has you playing as Ryan, a bartender, who has been suffering from nightmares, and eventually is drawn into a strange quest to become "the deliverer" and destroy the DreamWeb. While like other graphical adventure games you collect items and use them to solve puzzles, the viewpoint here is entirely overhead, which is an interesting switch but it provides certain challenges, like not always being able to see things clearly. To help overcome this the game does provide mouseover descriptions of items and a small "zoomed in" window in the lower corner. Definitely an intriguing and not too well known game. (This game was made freeware by its authors, as per the enclosed license.txt file.) Video ReviewVideo review of DreamWeb, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Excelsior Phase One: Lysandia
description: Excelsior is an innovative and in-depth RPG. It uses text-mode graphics with a custom character set, 2x1 tiles (your character and most objects are two characters wide) and even includes animated tiles. The story involves being a "Fixer" who travels between dimensions solving irregularities / problems as they occur. It plays like a typical old-style RPG, with turn-based battles, many items / weapons / armors / spells to acquire, and a huge world to explore. You create your character before starting the game, choosing their name, stats, and initial skills. This is a great game for RPG fans. The is a more modern Windows version of the game available on the company's website, where you can still buy the full version of their games. title: Tank Wars
description: Tank Wars (also known as BOMB due to the name of the zip file and it's executable file) is, as you might expect, a tank battle game. It is quite similar to the better-known game Scorched Earth which was released around the same time in the early 90's. The goal of the game is to destroy the other tank(s) controlled by human players or computer opponents (of varying intelligence levels) by selecting the angle and velocity of your shots. The game generates terrain of different formations for each level and includes wind as well (both typical of games in this genre, even the famous QBasic Gorillas game) as well as a ton of different configurable options. There are also different weapons that you can purchase between rounds. Generally a fun game of this genre. I have heard that the computer opponents' AI is tuned a bit better than Scorched Earth, so if you're looking to play against your PC (up to 10 simultaneously) this may be your best choice. Video ReviewVideo review of Tank Wars, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Albion
description: Albion is an innovative sci-fi RPG with some unique features and also a unique interface. Set in the year 2227, a scientist crash lands on a planet thought to be uninhabited, only to discover there is a rich variety of life there. You explore some areas in a traditional overhead 2D mode, while others in a first-person 3D mode. There are plenty of richly detailed environments to explore (this demo contains the first two scenarios from the full game) and plenty of NPCs to encounter and enemies to fight. The interface can be a bit tricky to get used to and many people dislike it. Nonetheless many consider it a forgotten classic in the RPG genre. WARNING: Playing DOSBOX_ALBIONFIX.ZIP on your own PC will likely not work. It is specifically set up for in-browser play. Download albion.zip and install the game locally instead. title: DOOM 2D
description: DISCLAIMER: First of all, if you're looking for the real 3D DOOM game from id Software, the game on this page is not by id Software and certainly not endorsed by them! (This is a sort of parody of the original DOOM.) Get the REAL original DOOM game here.Now then ... DOOM 2D is a strange experiment / parody (?) of the actual game. It was created by a Russian programming team and as you might expect, attempts to recreate the DOOM experience in a 2D platforming environment. It uses graphics and sound effects ripped from the official game. The controls are not bad, and there must have been considerable work that went into making it, with many different enemies, items, traps, even bosses and a two-player simultaneous mode. That said, I don't find it to be tremendously fun to play, so it seems to exist more for its novelty than anything else. (If you speak Russian, you may be interested in the included level editor. If not, it'd take considerable trial and error to figure out how it works!)

title: D/Generation
description: D/Generation is a unique isometic view action/puzzle game set in a large office building. You play a package delivery guy who gets trapped within the Genoq Biolabs facility when the security system goes berserk. The excellent graphics and playing style are both quite unique and the game's mix of puzzle and action gameplay work well together. (Tip: Press Alt-K to "rotate" the arrow keys 45 degrees to better facilitate isometic mode.) Clever touches abound, such as the computer terminals you find which explain parts of the story, and the weird things that people say when you rescue them. Clearly a lot of time and loving care went into crafting this game. This demo version gives you a preview of what the full game has to offer.

title: SEAL Team
description: SEAL Team is a Vietnam War strategy / action game. You control a single soldier, who gives orders to your teammates. As part of the team, you also move your own character, and attempt to complete the level's objective(s), such as killing all of the enemies, rescuing a hostage, or recovering an object. The game is presented from a third person perspective in full 3D using polygons to model the environments. (Supposedly using the same engine as 688 Attack Sub.) It looks impressive, but the action is a bit slower paced since this is supposed to be a sim / action hybrid type game. Definitely worth a look if you enjoy games of this sort.

You're in a maze, and you need to find and destroy the enemy generators, which spit out ASCII smiley-faced enemies that attack you. Not too intense of a game, but it has some interesting origins: It was apparently commissioned by Novell to test the networking capabilities of early LANs. So this game from 1982 has networked multiplayer capabilities, but don't ask me how to get it to work!

title: KBall
description: KBall is a beautifully designed ball-rolling game ala Marble Madness, but probably less stress-inducing than that classic game. It was originally released in 2003 but the DOS port was just made available in 2020. The goal is to collect all of the orbs then roll your ball to the exit. You'll need to be careful not to fall off the platform and move fast, because the timer is quickly ticking down. The game features great high-res graphics and several different level packs to try, including both easy beginner levels and challenging levels to frustrate even experienced players.

title: Tom & Jerry
description: Based on the popular cat and mouse cartoon characters, Tom and Jerry is a fun sidescrolling game. It is similar to what you might find on the Nintendo NES or Super Nintendo systems. The object is to hop through the levels, throwing balls at enemies to eliminate them and get to the exits. Well made EGA graphics and decent sound effects as well as pretty tight controls will make this a fun yet challenging game for fans of sidescrolling, jumping platform action. (The original developer released this game for free on their website.)

title: Hugo III: Jungle of Doom
description: The third and last game in the Hugo series which began with the much more widely-known Hugo's House of Horrors. This game takes place after a plane crash in the jungle, after which Penelope is bitten by a poisonous snake. It's again up to Hugo to save the day! The same game engine is used as the previous games, with a few tweaks, like a hints engine. Hugo's sprite will also change size as he moves farther into the background. The EGA graphics are generally quite good as this game brings the series to a close. It's safe to say that if you enjoyed the first two games, you'll likely enjoy the finale as well!

description: A very fun Pacman type game that expands on the original Pacman idea by adding different characters (Pacmen?) to play, as well as having varied, large levels and ghosts with individual personalities that talk to you between levels. The levels actually scroll so you can't see the entire playing area at once. Your Pacman can also jump and use new special items. With the scrolling playing field and jumping, it seems influenced by Pacmania. It's all very well done, and it's fun to play, as well.

title: Terminator: SkyNET
description: SkyNET (aka Terminator: SkyNET) is the final of three Terminator based FPS games that Bethesda released in the 90's. It was originally planned as an expansion pack for Terminator: Future Shock, SkyNET was released as a separate game, with an updated version of the 3D engine used. The game is pretty advanced for its time, with many different weapons, enemies, and even vehicles that you can drive. There are a lot of evil robots to destroy and plenty of things to shoot. The demo includes a single level of the 8 missions included in the full game, along with a single multiplayer map.

title: Beast
description: Beast is a simple ASCII-based game which doesn't have much of a story, but then it doesn't really need one. Your goal is to kill each of the "beasts" on each level (big letter "H"s). However, instead of weapons, you need to use the level itself to kill them, by trapping them between the pushable walls. Since it was made in 1984 it's graphics and sounds are extremely rudimentary, but its gameplay is fairly unique although it too is pretty simple. Not bad for a 19k file! (This game was mentioned in the book "The Video Game Explosion: A History from PONG to Playstation and Beyond" by Mark J. P. Wolf.)

title: 688 Attack Sub
description: 688 Attack Sub is a submarine simulation game, taking place during the cold war era. The player can perform various missions and can choose to control American or Soviet submarines. The focus here is on "realism" rather than action, and you'll need to learn the various different systems of the submarine in order to make progress. This demo version apparently came as some sort of bonus on Maxell diskettes, since there are constant references to Maxell during the game. (It even notes during the tutorial that certain features were omitted in this demo since they wouldn't it on the single floppy disk!) The demo does include a tutorial of sorts, although it doesn't explain how to play, just what the various options within the subsystems do. This is not my kind of game so I didn't invest too much time into trying to figure out what everything does. The graphics are decent for the time and it offers mouse control, and the full version offered multiplayer over modem, which I think was pretty good for the time period. I do remember that during grade school in the early 90's several of my friends were obsessed with this game so if you're into simulation war games give it a try.

title: Brutal: Paws of Fury
description: Brutal: Paws of Fury is a one-on-one fighting game in the style of Street Fighter and other similar fighting games from the 90's. Unlike most games of this style, the game has a cutesy-serious tone (is that a thing?) with anthropomorphic animals as its martial-artist protagonists. One advantage is that it's not too violent, so it'll be okay for younger kids to play it. The graphics are decent, with fast but not particularly smooth animations. As with most PC fighting games, doing the special moves (if you even know them) will be a challenge with the keyboard. The demo version offered here only provides two of the characters available in the full game.

title: Popcorn
description: Popcorn is a famous Arkanoid clone created in 1988 by a pair of French developers, Christophe Lacaze (code) and Frédérick (graphics/.sounds). This CGA Arkanoid clone was quite popular back in the early DOS days and was widely distributed online, for good reason! It plays quite well, and simulates most of the features of Arkanoid, albeit in CGA mode. The goal is the same: Break all the bricks on the level to progress. There are 50 levels in all, plus a level editor to create your own. The text of the game is in French but it's not too difficult to figure out what's what. (See Instructions for a list of all the function keys.) Note that pressing F9 toggles sound on/off! Full instructions in English can be found in the POP_ENG.DOC file translated by Phillip Bogle. (DOSBox is set to run in CGA mode, which displays the game with its intended RED color rather than the more typical CGA pink. If you're used to playing it in pink, run DOSBox in a VGA mode instead via the "machine" setting in dosbox.conf.) Video ReviewVideo review of Popcorn, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games
multiplayer: Up to 9 players, Turn based shared keyboard/mouse

title: Matrix
description: Matrix is a great Tetris variant which in most respects plays the same as the original game, but adds several options and variations, as well as presenting the game in a visually appealing yet still simple way. The basic gameplay is the same: Make lines by fitting falling pieces into the well. There are multiple speeds and handicaps to set, as well as "Scenarios" (which start with the well partially filled). You can record your playing session to watch again later, and you can also save your game and load it to continue at a later time. The controls work fluidly and since it offers many options it's a solid choice to play a game of Tetris!

title: Theme Hospital
description: Theme Hospital (1997) is the second in the "Theme ..." series of games following Theme Park in 1994. As you might expect, in this game you are given the task of running a hospital, including both the physical building layout, hiring staff, and providing for hospital guests. There are a number of different fictional diseases that need to be treated, and specialized rooms and equipment that can eventually be purchased for that purpose. The game's graphics and sounds are great, as to be expected in a Bullfrog Productions game. This demo version provides a tutorial as you get a taste of what the full game offers.

title: Megazeux
description: The best, most flexible game creation system created for MS-DOS, in my opinion. While it doesn't allow for the best graphics (it's in text mode, but you can edit the ASCII characters), it's extremely flexible, and it also allows Soundblaster music and sound effects. Games are created using a GUI to place various blocks, and programs are written using the built-in OOP Robotic programming language. title: X-COM: UFO Defense
description: X-COM is a series of turn-based strategy games, which means that I have never played or even been interested in playing them. However the series is much loved by fans of the genre, and this demo gives you a sample of what you'll find in the main game. The basic premise is ALIENS, and they're bad, so pew-pew-pew! You must lead your squad to gather intelligence, fight the aliens, and destroy their base. You issue commands to your various troops and they carry them out. As mentioned it's turn-based so you can carefully plan your moves. Graphics and sounds are good for the time it was released. It definitely has a professional, high quality feel. (Note: In the demo, this game is referred to as "X-COM: Terran Defense Force". This was a working title for the game before it was released. This game is also known as X-COM: Enemy Unknown in the UK and in some other places.)

title: Sango Fighter
description: Sango Fighter is a game that looks better than it actually plays. Inspired by the extremely popular Street Fighter series of games (and the dozens of clones that SF2 inspired) Sango Fighter likewise features detailed and interesting looking characters fighting in one-on-one combat. Each character has unique special moves; however they are not easy to pull off. The shareware version allows you to select one of five fighters, and play in tournament, battle, and two player vs modes. As stated above, although this game looks great. The sounds and music are decent as well. However the gameplay is a little choppy, and it's not too easy to pull off the characters' special moves. That, combined with only having 5 playable characters, make it much less fun than SF2 which it's emulating. Definitely worth trying out though as an example of what was possible in the early 90's DOS environment compared to the arcades of the era. (Sango Fighter features English, Chinese, and Japanese language options.) Video ReviewVideo review of Sango Fighter, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Highway Hunter
description: Highway Hunter is a vertical shooting game with great production values (animated cut-scenes, well-drawn SVGA graphics, parallax scrolling, great music) and intense action. In the game, you must drive along the futuristic roads and blast everything in your path. You will of course collect powerups to upgrade your weapons, and improved shields to protect your car. The fact that this game takes place on highway roads rather than in space means that your movement is a bit more restricted, and it makes the game stand out a bit more from other shmups. It's generally a top-notch shoot-em-up and shooting fans will definitely want to give it a try! Video ReviewVideo review of Highway Hunter, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Destruction Derby
description: Destruction Derby plays pretty much as you would expect: Crash your car into your opponents' cars, trying to cause as much damage to them as possible, while avoiding damage yourself. The game is presented in a rather impressive 3D mode which rivals the graphics of the early Playstation game console. (Not too surprising, I guess, since the game was also released for PS1 and other systems. It was even included on the recently released, poorly received Playstation Classic console.) The gameplay seems fun enough but, based on this limited demo, might not have a lot of depth to it. But it's definitely impressive to see it running smoothly in DOSBox.

title: Paranoid
description: Paranoid is another ball & paddle game. It features EGA graphics, PC speaker sound effects, and powerups to collect. The game is not particularly exciting to play, and part of that is due to the keyboard-only controls. Your paddle moves at a set speed, and you need to use the left and right shift keys to move. So you need to constantly be tracking the ball, otherwise you may not have time to get to it. The ball DOES bounce off the paddle differently depending where it hits, so that's a big plus. The designs of the levels don't seem particularly inspired, but at least it has a variety of powerups, although they should probably drop more often.

title: 4D Boxing
description: 4D Boxing attempts to recreate the sport of boxing more accurately than a lot of popular computer or arcade game based on the sport. It uses a graphics system that was, for the time, quite revolutionary; it was "created with TRU-MOTIONtm, an astonishing new technique that uses filled polygons to replicate human motion!" It's more like rock'em sock'em robot motion, but the game was nonetheless revolutionary for its time, and features decent graphics and sound effects, as well as complex controls which give you a lot of variety when maneuvering your fighter, and other simulation elements like boxer statistics. (Note: Run BOX.BAT to start the game.)

title: Mimi & the Mites
description: Hidden gem alert! Mimi & the Mites is a well-made platforming game where you must kill the mites and get to the exit. To do so, you'll need to shoot 'em, avoid 'em, and use various environmental tools like elevators, teleporters, and trampolines. The game features high production values with great graphics and animations, as well as music and sound effects. The levels are tricky but not too difficult (at least not the early ones) so it's a fun game that everyone should try. (The release status of this one is a bit strange, the title screen clearly states this is freeware, but a later release is clearly shareware, so I'm not sure exactly what the deal is here.)

title: Rise Of The Triad
description: A decent and relatively unknown FPS from Apogee. (Unknown compared to Wolf3D, DOOM, Duke, etc.) It's sort of in-between Wolf3D and Duke3D. It has some cool new features, such as choosing different characters at the beginning of the game, each of whom has unique abilities. But at times they don't seem to work together all that well. For example, there's too much platform jumping. Some people love this game, presumably due to its aesthetic, but I personally wasn't that excited about it. It doesn't feel as smooth as Doom. Some great ideas here though, and definitely unique. Video ReviewVideo review of Rise Of The Triad, courtesy of Ancient DOS Games

title: Mine Mayhem
description: Mine Mayhem is a great Minesweeper clone with many options which plays smoothly. In addition to the regular options you would find in Windows Minesweeper, Mine Mayhem also offers hexagonal shaped tiles, clear or "walk across" type gameplay, different levels of hint modes to help newer players, lots of statistics and high score tables, and a variety of configuration options to tweak the gameplay. Mouse support is of course included, and it controls the same as the familiar Windows version. Overall it's a great option for DOS Minesweeper and is highly recommended. Source code in C++ is also available.

title: Big Rig
description: Big Rig (no relation to the laughingly bad "Big Rigs: Over the Road Racing") is a text-mode truck driving simulation game. Your job is to safely transport your cargo to the destination. Similarly to games like Oregon Trail, you are given various decisions to make as the game progresses, like how fast to drive, how much fuel to buy, or whether or not to stop at a rest stop. The game is presented entirely in text, and there are no quick reflexes required. It seems like after playing a few times, you will begin to learn the tricks of making a successful delivery. Not terribly exciting but an interesting early (1986!) simulation game.

title: Spacewar
description: Do you like old games? What about the OLDEST game? Spacewar is generally credited with being the first video game, even before Pong. It was originally created in 1962 by Steve Russell at MIT. This DOS version was released much later, and recreates the original with some modifications. The game is essentially a 1-on-1 fight between two spaceships (2-players on one keyboard or you vs the computer). The graphics and so on are of course very primitive, but download this anyways to experience part of video games history.

description: Like Arkanoid ... except better! Described as "the ultimate Breakout", this Arkanoid "clone" isn't really a clone at all. It features great graphics, cool sounds, and varied level design. The best part, however, are the cool powerups that drop down. In some levels, the screen gets really crazy with all of the balls and powerups and enemies flying around. The only major complaint is that the ball bounces the same regardless of where it hits your paddle. This game was, many years later, remade as an app for modern mobile devices.

title: Mirror Magic
description: Mirror Magic is a puzzle game involving lasers and mirrors. It is, according to the author, a clone of the Commodore 64 game "Deflektor" and was originally released for the Amiga as "Mindbender". It's also been released for Windows and other platforms, and in fact that version is more up-to-date than the older DOS version provided here. Anyways, in each level, you have to adjust the various parts on screen via mouse input to use your laser ("magic beam") to collect the "magic kettles". The game comes with a set of pre-made levels, and you can make your own in the level editor. While this is not the kind of game I personally enjoy, it's undeniable that it's well made, with nicely drawn graphics and sound effects / music. The source code is provided in the ZIP file.

title: Battle Arena Toshinden
description: Battle Arena Toshinden is a well-known Playstation 1 3D fighting game. It was one of the first games I bought for my PS1. It's a Tekken-style one-on-one fighting game that involves mostly hand-to-hand combat and combos. Apparently a DOS port was also made of the game, and it's better than you might think, although not the same as the PS1 version even though it shares the same characters, moves, and controls. The controls are certainly one of the trickier parts, since using the keyboard to move around in 3D while trying to remember what all of the attack / block / etc buttons do can be challenging! It runs a little slowly as well, no doubt due to doing all of its 3D work without the aid of a 3D accelerator card. An impressive technical achievement if nothing else! This demo version contains 3 characters from the full version: Eiji, Sofia, and Mondo. Apparently Earthworm Jim is also a playable character in the full version?!

This game seems like it would still be a lot of fun for kids with its colorful graphics and interaction.

title: Kosmonaut
description: Kosmonaut is in some ways the prototype of a more advanced game, Skyroads. The title screen even seems to say "Skyroads" in an elaborate font. The concept is a 3D "racing" game where the only goal is to reach the end of the course. You do so by controlling your speed and jumping at the right moments. The game is tough, mainly because when you crash or fall off the track, it mocks you and then you have to start over! But it's an interesting first concept that was developed more fully in later games. (We can also see how this game influenced modern games, such as Snail Mail for iPhone/iPad.)

title: Peter Pan: A Story Painting Adventure
description: Peter Pan: A Story Painting Adventure is a simple game aimed at young children. You control Peter Pan as he goes on an adventure and encounters a variety of different challenges. You interact by choosing an action that one of the four "Paintbox Pals" at the bottom of the screen suggests to help Peter get out of trouble. title: Drug Wars: A Game Based on the New York Drug Market
description: Written by a high school student and sometimes referred to as the "original GTA", the game has really nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto, and more to do with a stock market type simulation game that happens to have the theme of a drug dealer. In the game, you are given $2,000, and you need to buy and sell drugs to turn that into at least $5,500 to pay off your debt. As you move to different areas, time progresses, random events may occur, and the prices of the drugs changes. The game is presented in a distinct text mode system in monochrome, so you'll have to use your imagination. This game served as the inspiration for several other similar games, and was played by countless kids in high school IT labs back in the day.

title: Subhunt
publisher: Laboratory for Recreational Computing at the University of North Texas
description: Subhunt is an interesting submarine mission simulation game developed by a group at a university game development lab: Laboratory for Recreational Computing at the University of North Texas, which still exists today. Apparently it was coded entirely from scratch using no existing libraries in C++ and Assembly. Anyways, it's a submarine simulator, so there are lots of buttons and things to press, and you'll need to spend some time learning how everything works because this is not an arcade-type sim. It does provide you with a 3D-rendered view outside your sub. The full game contains 12 missions but only one is included in the shareware game.

title: Revenge of the Mutant Camels
description: A side-scrolling platforming shooting game from Jeff Minter's Llamasoft? It must be incredibly zany! With a name like Revenge of the Mutant Camels, that's pretty much a given. Here you pilot your goat riding a mutant camel as it runs from left to right, shooting in whichever direction you last moved, sorta like a Robotron / Llamatron platforming game. Things attack you from all angles and you try to retain your sanity as you try to shoot them. Graphics and sounds are also suitably zany. It's definitely an interesting experience but I personally didn't find it particularly fun to play!

title: Putt-Putt Joins the Parade
description: Putt-Putt Joins the Parade is the first in a long series of Putt-Putt games which are still being released over 20 years later. The game is an edutainment product in the "Junior Adventures" line that was popular in the 90's when it was first released, and continues to live on through re-releases on iOS, Android, and Steam. You play the titular car, Putt-Putt, who wants to join the parade. But first he must earn cash to pay for a car wash, among other assorted tasks. There are plenty of things for kids to click on which result in little animation / sound flourishes. The game is designed to use speech instead of text (good for younger players) so be sure to turn on your speakers.

It was originally authored by Will Crowther in 1976, then expanded in 1977 with the help of Don Woods. In it you must type in commands to move through various locations and solve puzzles. For lots more info on this game, plus dozens of other versions of the game for DOS and many other platforms, visit Baf's Interactive Fiction Guide: Adventure!)

title: Mortal Kombat 3
description: This demo pre-release version of Mortal Kombat 3 allows you to play as either Jax or Sheeva in a 1-player vs computer, or 2-player match. This is of course the third in the long-running series of MK games, known for their violent fatalities and signature gameplay which fighting game fans often either love or hate. This third installment looks and feels very similar to the arcade game, which is no small feat on MS-DOS in 1995. Although only two characters are playable here, you can get a feel for the game, including the characters' special moves. The main limitation to playing it in DOS is using the keyboard to play, with the default keys (arrow keys plus the Insert-Del-PgUp-PgDn keys as your attack keys) being rather difficult to use. Modern solutions like Joy2Key can help make this game easier to play. The full version is available from GOG.com in a set with games 1 & 2 of the series for a reasonable price.

title: Nethack
description: Despite it's name, this game does NOT involve any type of computer "hacking". It's actually my favorite "Roguelike" game, orignally based on the "Hack" roguelike. While it may take awhile to learn all of the different commands, the game itself is very deep and involving. Plus, it's different each time you play. Unlike most Roguelikes, Nethack also features optional VGA graphics. This is one of the few games that I come back to play over and over, so I suggest you try it! (Check nethack.org for ports for Windows, Linux, and many more systems.)

title: Tempest 2000
description: Tempest is a vector-based action / shooting arcade game that was released in 1981. Your ship rotates around the tubular playing field and shoots the enemies as they approach towards the screen. This updated version was released in 1994, with similar gameplay and a freshly updated design by Jeff Minter of Llamasoft fame. (It is known as one of the few good games released primarily for the Atari Jaguar system!) The graphics and sounds ratchet up the intensity level, with pixelated explosions and cycling colors complimenting the smooth vector-like animations. Safe to say that if you enjoyed the original you will like this updated version, presented here in demo form.

title: The Last Eichhof
description: The Last Eichhof is a decent game with an ... uh, "original" premise? In this space shooting game, you play a beer floating in space. Yeah, like a bottle of beer. You must shoot down all of the enemies (like kegs and stuff) using an unlimited supply of bottle caps and save the universe (I guess ... why not ...) from big corporations. Aside from the premise, the game does have decent production values, with lots of music and sound effects, and decent graphics with plenty of animation and smooth effects. You can also buy upgrades between levels. (Note that to exit the store you must move ALL THE WAY LEFT to the green EXIT marker! It took me too long to figure that out ...)

description: Not that bad at all. This is a game that Apogee released between Wolfenstein 3D and Rise of the Triad. Basically it uses the Wolfenstien engine with some modifications, the best of which is a map so you're not lost throughout the entire game. It also adds a greater variety of enemies, money which can be used to buy things, switches which change the level, and so on. It isn't quite as memorable as Wolf3D (mostly because it lacks the freshness of that game) but if you like the older 3D games like Wolf3D or Catacomb Abyss you might want to try it out. description: The best tank war game I've ever seen. It's called 'The Mother of all games' by the author and was chosen as PC World magazine as the third best DOS game of all time. In it, you are competing against up to 10 other tanks (controlled by other players or by the computer) and you battle by entering a velocity and turret angle before firing off various weapons, which you can purchase between rounds. title: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar
description: Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar is, unsurprisingly, the fourth in the famous and influential Ultima series of fantasy RPGs. In 1996 Computer Gaming World placed Ultima IV #2 on its "Best PC Games of All Time", and for good reason. Ultima 4 is considered a big step forward for the series, and for computer role-playing games in general. The world of Britannia is fleshed out more than the first three games and there is a lot more story and personality evident in the game and the world itself. Although the graphics are crude by today's standards, it's the gameplay of story, exploration, battles (using a great environmentally-aware battle system) and character customization that make the game a true classic. Worth playing for RPG fans, but take note that since it was made in 1987 this is a true hardcore old-school RPG with no hand holding that will take considerable effort to learn and get into! (Note that the full version of the game along with full manuals and other extras is available via GOG.com; free registration is required to download and play it.)
